pull_request.title: Add bounded fallible fixture-cell admission on Memory 0.44
pull_request.body:
Reconcile bounded fixture admission from this PR and typed setup/memory transfer from #116 against released Memory 0.44.0. Refs #104; supersedes #116 once this refreshed contribution is available for review.

`test-support` adds typed setup/write refusal, explicit bounded fresh/retained entry points and admitted-memory transfer. Retained headers, capacity and selected byte limits are checked before Cell loads its payload; invalid retained bytes are never initialized as fresh. Existing `new`/`set` keep their panic convention. The temporary runtime is dropped after authority verification and opening, retaining only the cell/handle and its ceiling. Codecs, initialization and lifecycle remain caller-owned. Bootstrap can advance allocation-ledger metadata before later Cell refusal; backing IO and publication can still panic.

The one header-admission helper serves both fixtures and the unchanged bounded ledger reader. There is no dependency or stored-format change. Pending notes select compatible 0.44.1 without changing package versions or lockfiles.

Validation on the reconciled source: 197 library tests pass (six explicit allocation measurements remain ignored); all eight fixture tests pass, including retained-header preservation, header-only oversized refusal, bounded writes, short replacement and missing Cell admission. Strict feature Clippy, warning-denied feature Rustdoc, formatting, Rust 1.91 native/all-target and Wasm checks, and current-toolchain feature Wasm compilation pass. All five default-feature raw Wasm probes have no size increase: core −97 bytes, diagnostics unchanged in size, admission −105, runtime integration −91 and installed IO −91.

Full release validation, installed qualification of this new head and native macOS acceptance were not run locally. Required hosted checks remain separate. Blob, Jobs and Auth adoption still requires this extension to be integrated/published and qualified by those consumers; their earlier-source evidence is not current adoption.
